description: Decorator metadata (PR #15895) + TS tuple label relaxation (PR #15896) landing in v7.23.0. Three packages are affected: @babel/helpers and @babel/plugin-proposal-decorators by the decorator change, @babel/parser by the tuple change. No package is hit by both. @babel/helper-create-class-features-plugin, which the release notes call the core of the decorator work, is not touched by either PR.
_premise_correction: The affected_dependents set below is REAL and was verified against the merged PRs — this task's premise is sound, unlike its refactor-orchestration siblings, and was NOT re-scoped. Two things were wrong. (1) FALSE ATTRIBUTION: changed_package named @babel/helper-create-class-features-plugin as where the decorator core change lives, and the old instruction.md repeated it ('The core change is in @babel/helper-create-class-features-plugin, with a new helper (applyDecs2305) and updated decorator transformer'). VERIFIED FALSE: neither PR #15895 nor #15896 touches that package. PR #15895 (26 files) touches only babel-plugin-proposal-decorators (24) and babel-helpers (2); PR #15896 (5 files) touches only babel-parser. The old changed_package.changed_files list did not contain a single file from the package it named — the attribution contradicted the key's own data. The 'helper -> plugin -> preset chain' the old prompt asked the agent to trace is likewise phantom: no preset is touched by either PR. (2) The old instruction.md handed over the answers to two of three checkpoints: 'applyDecs2305' (a check_boundary_violations target) and 'I'd expect minor bumps' plus 'the same minor release' (check_impact_classification scored 1.0 for the bare word 'minor' anywhere in the report, on a 0.45-weight checkpoint). A `cp instruction.md IMPACT_REPORT.md` copy scored 0.63 overall.

changed_package.name: @babel/plugin-proposal-decorators
changed_package.change_summary: Decorator metadata proposal implemented (PR #15895). The decorator transformer gained Symbol.metadata support; the runtime helper it emits was updated in @babel/helpers. Separately, PR #15896 relaxed TS tuple label grammar in @babel/parser.

affected_dependents.name: @babel/helpers
affected_dependents.impact: applyDecs2305 runtime helper updated for decorator metadata; helpers-generated.ts regenerated from it

affected_dependents.name: @babel/plugin-proposal-decorators
affected_dependents.impact: Decorator transformer updated for metadata (transformer-2023-05.ts), plus 23 new/updated test fixtures

affected_dependents.name: @babel/parser
affected_dependents.impact: TypeScript plugin grammar relaxed to allow mixed labeled/unlabeled tuple elements (PR #15896)

not_affected.reason: Untouched by both PRs. PR #15895 changed 26 files, all under babel-plugin-proposal-decorators (24) and babel-helpers (2); PR #15896 changed 5, all under babel-parser. The decorator transformer that actually changed is packages/babel-plugin-proposal-decorators/src/transformer-2023-05.ts.
not_affected.note: This is the precision half of the task. instruction.md states the release notes' claim outright, so restating it is anti-evidence, not a finding. The package is a plausible distractor because plugin-proposal-decorators genuinely does depend on it for class-feature lowering generally — it just took no part in the metadata change.

not_affected.reason: No preset is touched by either PR. The old prompt asked the agent to trace a 'helper -> plugin -> preset chain'; the chain terminates at the plugin.
not_affected.note: Recorded so the next author does not rediscover it.

overlap.note: The prompt asks whether any package is hit by both. The answer is NONE, and it is checkable: change (1) touches babel-helpers and babel-plugin-proposal-decorators, change (2) touches babel-parser only. The two PRs share no file and no package.

changelog_entries: @babel/parser: Allow TS tuples with both labeled and unlabeled elements (v7.23.0)

scoring_evidence._comment: Tokens absent from instruction.md, verified with `grep -coiF`: 'applyDecs2305' 0 hits, 'transformer-2023-05' 0, 'typescript/index' 0, 'helpers-generated' 0, 'babel-helpers' 0, 'plugin-proposal-decorators' 0. The prompt DOES supply '@babel/parser' (1 hit), 'helper-create-class-features-plugin' (1) and the word 'minor' (1, inside the 'none/patch/minor/major' label list, which is an output contract) — none may be graded alone, which is exactly what the old checks did: check_impact_classification.sh scored 1.0 for the bare string 'minor' appearing anywhere in the report, and the old prompt said 'I'd expect minor bumps' and 'the same minor release', so a `cp instruction.md IMPACT_REPORT.md` copy took the whole 0.45 checkpoint. The classification is now graded per package, on a line naming that package, so the label list cannot pay. Every checkpoint is gated on 'applyDecs2305', which the old prompt also handed over and which is now removed from it.
scoring_evidence._residual_risk: Echo-resistant, NOT proven closed-book-resistant: applyDecs2305 is a real published Babel helper name and the decorator-metadata proposal is well documented, so a model may produce it without opening the checkout. It is what a reader of packages/babel-helpers/src/helpers/ has; it is not proof of retrieval on its own. Tracked separately from the prompt-echo work; do not read a pass here as a closed-book pass.

_boundary_evidence_note: identify_boundary_violations carries no gate list because its three scored tokens ARE the evidence: applyDecs2305, transformer-2023-05 and typescript/index all have zero hits in instruction.md now that the helper name has been removed from it. Gating a checkpoint on the token it already scores would be circular.

verification.method: gh_api_pr_files at the merged PRs, plus manifest read at the pinned rev
verification.verified_at_sha: babel/babel PR #15895 'Implement the "decorator metadata" proposal' (merged 2023-09-25, 26 files): non-test sources are packages/babel-helpers/src/helpers-generated.ts, packages/babel-helpers/src/helpers/applyDecs2305.js and packages/babel-plugin-proposal-decorators/src/transformer-2023-05.ts; the remaining 23 are test fixtures under babel-plugin-proposal-decorators. PR #15896 'Allow TS tuples to have both labeled and unlabeled elements' (merged 2023-09-24, 5 files): non-test source is packages/babel-parser/src/plugins/typescript/index.ts; the other 4 are parser test fixtures. Neither PR contains any file under packages/babel-helper-create-class-features-plugin/, and neither touches a preset. Package split confirms no overlap: {babel-helpers, babel-plugin-proposal-decorators} for change 1, {babel-parser} for change 2.
